_schema: One JSON object per line. Fields: timestamp (ISO 8601), section (NN), paragraph (int, 1-based), claim_text (string, max 200 chars), support_type (evidence-card | footnote | unmapped), support_ref (path to evidence card OR footnote number OR null), reason (string, only present when support_type=unmapped, one of: evidence-gap | not-yet-harvested | requires-primary-source | intentional-conjecture), audited_in_run (int, the run_count when this claim was first audited), confidence (float 0-1, agent's confidence in the mapping). Initial seed entry below; the verify-provenance sub-task appends one entry per claim per section per audit run.

claim_text: The LMS files arrive in a learning-management folder as a flat list organized only by name.
Expert review is built into the process at defined checkpoints where the professor inspects, corrects, and gates whether the work advances.
The case study is a reviewed static website, not a conversational agent or chatbot placed in front of students.
The article makes no claim that students learned more, because it has not run the study that would license such a claim.
The case study became a live knowledge system of 198 pages: 92 case briefs, 27 doctrinal topic pages, and 79 lecture summaries.
The case study is published at https://constitutionallaw.netlify.app and is readable by anyone (URL verified live).
Each case page is written against the indexed judicial opinion rather than a paraphrase, so a quotation traces to the controlling source.
The doctrinal scope is the structural constitution (judicial review, federalism, separation of powers, commerce power, executive authority, justiciability, Reconstruction amendments).
note: mapped but scope characterization inconsistent with Section IV.A; see PI-118
